question: Should OpenClaw elevate `message_sending` into the fail-closed universal outbound policy boundary, or introduce a new versioned outbound policy API with explicit trusted-plugin and audit semantics?
rationale: Source inspection proves remaining bypass and fail-open paths, but only maintainer product/security intent can decide the permanent contract for hook failures, plugin authority, audit metadata, and which outbound sends are in scope.

options.title: Design a versioned policy API
options.body: Create a dedicated outbound policy contract that can be fail-closed, audited, scoped, and documented without overloading the existing best-effort hook semantics.

options.title: Elevate message_sending
options.body: Make `message_sending` the universal exactly-once fail-closed gate and migrate all direct delivery paths onto that contract.

options.title: Keep hooks advisory
options.body: Document that strict DLP/compliance enforcement is not guaranteed by the current hook surfaces and keep the remaining work out of core for now.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned policy API
recommendation.body: Create a dedicated outbound policy contract that can be fail-closed, audited, scoped, and documented without overloading the existing best-effort hook semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and prior review history place this person closest to the broad hook/security decision surface.
